# Principal Rotations in 3D Space

## Definition

Principal rotations are rotations about the **three coordinate axes** (x, y, and z), forming the fundamental building blocks of all spatial rotations.

---

## The Three Principal Rotation Matrices

### Rotation about X-axis by angle θ:
$$R_x(\theta) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ 0 & \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{bmatrix}$$

### Rotation about Y-axis by angle θ:
$$R_y(\theta) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & 0 & \sin\theta \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -\sin\theta & 0 & \cos\theta \end{bmatrix}$$

### Rotation about Z-axis by angle θ:
$$R_z(\theta) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta & 0 \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

---

## Decomposition of Any Spatial Rotation

Any rotation **R** can be expressed as a composition of principal rotations:

$$R = R_z(\alpha) \cdot R_y(\beta) \cdot R_x(\gamma)$$

where α, β, γ are called **Euler angles**.

---

## Important Properties

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **Non-commutativity** | $R_x R_y \neq R_y R_x$ in general |
| **Group closure** | Composition of rotations is a rotation |
| **Invertibility** | $R(\theta)^{-1} = R(-\theta)$ |
| **Orthogonality** | $R^T = R^{-1}$, det(R) = +1 |

---

## Corrections to the Original Answer

> ⚠️ The original answer contains inaccuracies:

1. **"Axis-angle" representation** is *not* the same as Euler angle decomposition — axis-angle uses a **single axis and one angle**
2. **2D principal rotations** involve only **one axis** (z-axis perpendicular to the plane), not two
3. The decomposition order **matters** due to non-commutativity

---

## Key Takeaway

$$\boxed{R_{arbitrary} = R_z(\alpha) \cdot R_y(\beta) \cdot R_x(\gamma)}$$

This decomposition is fundamental in **robotics**, **aerospace** (roll/pitch/yaw), **computer graphics**, and **physics**.
